from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Start with a base and exponent.", "Visualize growth as a tree.", "Example: 2 raised to 3 is 8."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: The Exponential Foundation", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show label 'Base: b' in #FFFFFF at left, exponent 'x' in #FFCC00
        base_label = Text("Base: b", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(base_label, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(base_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        exp_label = Text("Exponent: x", color="#FFCC00")
        self.place_at_grid(exp_label, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(exp_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualize growth as a tree
        tree = VGroup(
            Triangle(color=GREEN).scale(0.5),
            Line(ORIGIN, DOWN*0.5, color=GREY_BROWN).next_to(ORIGIN, DOWN, buff=0)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(tree, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(DrawBorderThenFill(tree))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Example: 2 raised to 3 is 8.
        # Animate result 'y' in #00FFCC appearing to the right.
        # Draw arrow connecting base/exponent to result.
        # Flash the full expression: b^x = y.
        eq = MathTex("2^3 = 8", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(eq, "E3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(eq))
        
        y_label = Text("Result: y", color="#00FFCC")
        self.place_at_grid(y_label, "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(y_label))
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFCC")
        self.play(Indicate(eq))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Roots are just inverse growth.", "Roots are fractional exponents.", "Example: Square root of 9 is 9^(1/2)."]
        self.setup_layout("Roots as Fractional Exponents", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Roots are just inverse growth.
        # Display radical 'sqrt(n, x)' in #FF99FF.
        radical = MathTex(r"\sqrt[n]{x}", color="#FF99FF")
        self.place_at_grid(radical, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(radical))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF99FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Roots are fractional exponents.
        # Show conversion: sqrt(n, x) = x^(1/n) in #FFFFFF.
        conversion = MathTex(r"\sqrt[n]{x} = x^{1/n}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(conversion, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Transform(radical, conversion))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Example: Square root of 9 is 9^(1/2).
        # Highlight the exponent '1/n' in #FFCC00.
        example = MathTex(r"\sqrt{9} = 9^{1/2}", color=WHITE)
        # Highlight exponent part
        # Note: MathTex indexing can be tricky, relying on visual confirmation
        # Simply replacing with colored exponent for highlighting
        example_highlight = MathTex(r"\sqrt{9} = 9^{", r"1/2", r"}", color=WHITE)
        example_highlight.set_color_by_tex("1/2", "#FFCC00")
        
        self.place_at_grid(example_highlight, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(example_highlight))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFCC00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Logarithms act as detectives.",
            "They hunt for missing exponents.",
            "Log_b(x) = y finds the exponent.",
            "Example: 3^4 = 81 means log_3(81) = 4.",
            "Logs bridge powers and roots."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Logarithms: Seeking the Exponent", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        log_eq = MathTex(r"\log_b(x) = y", font_size=48)
        pow_eq = MathTex(r"b^y = x", font_size=48)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Write(log_eq))
        self.place_at_grid(log_eq, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        highlight_x = Circle(color=YELLOW, radius=0.3).move_to(log_eq[0][4])
        self.play(Create(highlight_x))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.play(FadeOut(highlight_x))
        self.place_at_grid(pow_eq, 'D4', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(pow_eq))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(RED)
        example = MathTex(r"3^4 = 81 \implies \log_3(81) = 4", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(example, 'F3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(example))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(PURPLE)
        self.play(FadeOut(log_eq), FadeOut(pow_eq), FadeOut(example))
        conclusion = Text("Logs bridge the Gap!", font_size=36, color=PURPLE)
        self.place_at_grid(conclusion, 'C3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visual Synthesis: The Transformation Map", [
            "Use our triangular relationship map.",
            "Powers, roots, logs are linked.",
            "Rotate views to see connections.",
            "2^3=8 connects these three forms.",
            "Perspectives change, the math stays."
        ])
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0.1, 4, 1], y_range=[0.1, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFCC")
        exp_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: 2**x, color="#00FFCC")
        self.play(Create(exp_graph))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF99FF")
        log_graph = axes.plot(lambda x: np.log2(x), color="#FF99FF")
        self.play(Create(log_graph))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        line_xy = axes.plot(lambda x: x, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2, stroke_opacity=0.5)
        self.play(Create(line_xy))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(3, 8), color=YELLOW) # 2^3=8
        # wait, the axes range is only 0.1-4. 2^3=8 is off chart.
        # Let's use 2^1=2 for visibility.
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(1, 2), color=YELLOW)
        label = Text("2^1=2", font_size=18, color=YELLOW).next_to(point, UP)
        self.play(Create(point), Write(label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Quick-Check", [
            "Everything is connected.", 
            "Powers, roots, logs, one family.", 
            "Convert 5^2=25 to log_5(25)=2."
        ])
        
        # Define table content
        table = VGroup(
            Text("Operation", color=BLUE), Text("Relationship", color=BLUE),
            Text("Exponential", color=WHITE), Text("Base^Exp = Power", color=WHITE),
            Text("Logarithmic", color=WHITE), Text("log_Base(Power) = Exp", color=WHITE)
        ).arrange_in_grid(rows=3, cols=2, buff=0.5)
        
        self.place_in_area(table, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFCC00"))
        self.play(FadeIn(table))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFCC00"))
        # Highlight relationship
        self.play(table.animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFCC00"))
        # Quick quiz example
        quiz = MathTex("5^2 = 25", "\\implies", "\\log_5(25) = 2", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(quiz, "E3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(quiz))

outline.topic: The Universal Language of Exponents: Bridging Powers, Roots, and Logarithms

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Exponential Foundation
sections.content: Define a base 'b' and an exponent 'x'. Visualize the power operation as a 'growth tree' where b is the seed and x is the number of replications (b^x = y).
sections.example: Visualize 2^3 as a colony of rabbits: Start with 2, doubling 3 times results in 8 rabbits.

sections.title: Roots as Fractional Exponents
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'inverse growth'. Explain that a root is simply an exponent that is a fraction. If x is the power, 1/x is the root. Graphically show the shift from building a pyramid (power) to finding its dimensions (root).
sections.example: The square root of 9 is 9^(1/2). Imagine a square plot of land with area 9; the side length is the 'root'—exactly 3.

sections.title: Logarithms: Seeking the Exponent
sections.content: Introduce logs as the 'detective' of the mathematical world. While powers find the total, logarithms find the missing time/generations. Formula: If b^y = x, then log_b(x) = y.
sections.example: If a bacterial culture triples every hour (3^y = 81), the logarithm log_3(81) tells us it took 4 hours to reach that count.

sections.title: Visual Synthesis: The Transformation Map
sections.content: Present a 'Triangular Relationship' diagram connecting these three notations. This is the 'Golden Rule' of exponential movement. Show how moving between these forms is just rotating the perspective on the same equation.
sections.example: The relationship 2^3=8 can be viewed as: Power (2^3=8), Root (8^(1/3)=2), or Log (log_2(8)=3).

sections.title: Summary & Quick-Check
sections.content: A 30-second wrap-up. Emphasize that these are not different math topics, but different ways to view the same exponential relationship.
sections.example: Final quiz: Convert 5^2 = 25 into logarithmic notation. (Answer: log_5(25) = 2).
